chunks: And Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Sayābah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said:
The testimony of one who rushes ahead of the pilgrims is not accepted, for he has destroyed his mount, exhausted his provisions, wearied himself, and treated his salat (prayer) lightly.
It was said: What about the muleteer, the camel driver, and the sailor?
So he said: There is no harm in them; their testimony is accepted if they are righteous.

key_terms.الْجَمَّالُ: a camel driver or camel owner who transports goods or people
key_terms.سَابِقِ الْحَاجِّ: one who rushes ahead of the pilgrims in travel
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his salat (prayer), whose neglect reflects poor conduct

ai.seo_question: When is a person's testimony rejected or accepted in Shia hadith law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the acceptance of testimony, distinguishing between blameworthy haste in hajj travel and ordinary travel occupations. It indicates that a person's conduct, especially negligence toward salat (prayer) and reckless behavior, affects judicial credibility, while the testimony of workers such as transporters and sailors is accepted when they are righteous.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3297 - And it was narrated by Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Ala' ibn Sayabah, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said that Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), said:
"The testimony of one who hastens ahead of the pilgrims is not accepted, as he has killed his mount, consumed his provisions, exhausted himself, and neglected his prayers."
It was asked: "What about the muleteer, the camel driver, and the sailor?"
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in them; their testimony is accepted if they are righteous."
